prompt: A ribbon is $6$ feet long. It is cut into pieces that are each $\frac{3}{4}$ foot long. How many pieces are there?
hint: You are asked how many equal short lengths fit into the full ribbon. Which operation answers a "how many fit" question?

hints.text: You are asked how many equal short lengths fit into the full ribbon. Which operation answers a "how many fit" question?

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Every $3$ feet gives $4$ pieces (since $4 \times \frac{3}{4} = 3$). How many 3-foot chunks are in 6 feet?
Divide $6$ by $\frac{3}{4}$. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, so work out $6 \times \frac{4}{3}$.

explanation: The number of pieces is how many times $\frac{3}{4}$ foot fits into $6$ feet, which is $6 \div \frac{3}{4}$.
Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal: $6 \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{24}{3} = 8$.
Check by multiplying back: $8 \times \frac{3}{4} = 6$ feet, so there are $8$ pieces.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count by chunks
steps: $6$ feet is two of those chunks: $2 \times 4 = 8$ pieces.
